title: AdaptiveFL: Adaptive Heterogeneous Federated Learning for Resource-Constrained AIoT Systems
problem: Federated Learning on AIoT devices suffers from low classification performance due to heterogeneity in computing capacity and memory size across devices, combined with uncertain operating environments that impact model convergence.
motivation: Resource-constrained AIoT devices need effective collaborative learning mechanisms that adapt to their heterogeneous capabilities for practical edge deployment.
method: The system creates smaller versions of the AI model by removing unimportant connections (called width-wise pruning), producing different model sizes for different devices. It uses reinforcement learning—a machine learning technique that learns by trying different options and improving—to automatically choose which model size each device should use based on its processing power and available memory. Each device then trains its assigned model locally on its own data.
key_novelty: The core insight is using neural network pruning combined with reinforcement learning to automatically assign right-sized models to each resource-constrained device in a federated learning system.
contributions: Fine-grained width-wise model pruning mechanism for generating heterogeneous device-specific models
RL-based adaptive device selection and model assignment strategy
Up to 8.94% inference accuracy improvement demonstrated on both IID and non-IID scenarios
primary_theme: adaptive federated learning for heterogeneous edge devices
